transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… yeah, I came in because things have felt kind of out of control lately. I’d just moved into a new apartment and I could barely get settled—like boxes everywhere, couldn’t really get my footing—and then suddenly I was saying yes to all these mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and deciding I needed to redesign my entire portfolio.

It was like… I don’t know, like I had to fix my whole life in one sprint. Which is funny because I do interface design, so everything becomes a “sprint” in my head, even my closet, apparently. But it stopped feeling normal, I guess. That’s why I’m here.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your mood over the past few weeks?

Yeah… definitely. Earlier this month I had these stretches where I felt almost electric, like weirdly upbeat and ready to take on everything, and then I’d flip over something tiny.

Like, a contractor would be late getting back to me about some apartment thing, or my sister would ask a normal question, and I’d snap like they were personally trying to block me. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud. I mean, delays are delays, right? Everyone has them. But in the moment it felt huge, like they were in the way of this whole plan I had in my head.
During those times when you felt electric and upbeat, did you feel like you could accomplish anything you set your mind to?

I’m not totally sure I’d put it as “anything,” exactly. It felt more like… I’d look at my whole life like it was a messy homepage and think, okay, I can clean all of this up if I just start moving fast enough.

But then, sorry, that makes me think of this one client who always wants everything “streamlined,” and it’s like, what does that even mean when they have seventeen menu items? Anyway. Um. I guess I felt unusually capable, yeah, but I don’t know if it was like some big “I’m unstoppable” thing. It was more like I couldn’t see why I shouldn’t take on a lot at once.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah… sleep’s been pretty bad. I’ll get into bed and then I’m just lying there replaying everything I think I messed up that day, like my brain opens fifty tabs and refuses to close them.

Or I’ll fall asleep for a bit and then wake up around four in the morning because of the traffic outside—my new place is louder than I expected, which is another whole thing with the windows—and once I’m awake, I can’t get my brain quiet again. It just starts running.
Did you feel unusually important or special during those times when you felt electric and upbeat?

I don’t think so… not “important” or “special” exactly. I mean, I probably acted like my projects were suddenly urgent, like everyone needed to respond right away, but that’s more me getting wrapped up in it.

Special makes me think of, like, some award ceremony or those LinkedIn posts where people say they’re “humbled” but then it’s a whole paragraph about how amazing they are. I don’t think I was feeling like that. More just… keyed up and overly convinced the stuff I was doing mattered right then.
Have you had any periods where you felt really down or depressed recently?

Yeah… I mean, lately I’ll wake up and there’s just this heavy, gray feeling sitting in my chest. It’s not always tied to anything obvious, which almost makes it weirder.

Like the apartment can be totally quiet, nothing is technically wrong, and then I’ll see a coffee mug in the sink and feel like I could just start crying over it. Which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, because it’s just a mug, and I know I could wash it in ten seconds, but in the moment it feels… I don’t know, like proof that everything is too much.
When you took on all those extra projects and mentoring sessions, were you hoping to achieve something specific by doing so?

Yeah, I think I was trying to… fix everything, maybe? Like if I could just become this super-productive version of myself, then the rest of my life would sort of snap into place.

I had barely even settled into the new apartment—there were still boxes around, and I kept meaning to buy curtains, which somehow turned into looking at fourteen different window treatment websites—and then suddenly I was saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and redesigning my entire portfolio. It felt like I needed to get my whole life sorted in one sprint, like a work sprint, not running. Though honestly running probably would’ve been healthier.

So, yeah, I guess the “specific” thing was proving I could get everything back on track all at once.
Have you been having trouble focusing on one task for a long period of time?

I’m not totally sure. I mean… sometimes I think I’m focusing, but then I’ll realize I’ve had the same design file open for ages and I’ve mostly been rearranging tiny things that probably don’t matter. Like moving a button two pixels and then wondering if the whole page needs a different color palette, and then somehow I’m looking up lamps for the apartment because the screen feels too bright.

So… maybe? But I don’t know if that counts as “trouble focusing for a long time” or just me being bad at staying with one lane when my brain starts making side roads.
How long do these periods of feeling electric and upbeat, followed by feeling down or depressed, typically last?

I guess the whole up-and-down thing has been happening since I moved into this apartment, so… about a month? It’s hard to separate it neatly, because moving kind of messes with time anyway—like I still have a box labeled “kitchen” that somehow has scarves in it—but yeah, the intense electric/upbeat stretches and then the crashy, gray ones have been cycling around for roughly the past month.
Do these periods of feeling electric and upbeat, or down and depressed, seem to be triggered by specific events or do they seem to happen on their own?

I’m not sure I’ve spotted a clear trigger, honestly. Sometimes I think it’s tied to something, like an email coming in or having a good idea for a page layout, but then other times it just… shows up, and I’m already in it before I’ve figured out why.

It’s hard to tell because life has had a lot of background noise lately, you know? Like moving stuff around, trying to make the apartment feel less temporary, and then I’ll start thinking the apartment is the reason, but then I remember I was also feeling weirdly charged while doing completely normal things, like making coffee or choosing fonts. So… I don’t know. I haven’t noticed one specific thing that reliably sets it off.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since you started experiencing these mood swings?

Yeah… I think so. I’ve kind of been pulling back from people, which is not great. Like, friends will text and I’ll see it, and then I think, “I’ll answer when I sound normal,” and then suddenly it’s three days later and now it feels weird to answer at all.

And with family too, I’ve been avoiding calls a bit because I feel embarrassed. I already feel like I’ve been scattered and unreliable lately, and I don’t really want to explain that. I even missed a design review at work, which was… really mortifying, and somehow that made me want to hide from everyone more. Like if I don’t talk to people, they won’t notice how all over the place I am, except obviously that’s not how relationships work.
Are these mood swings affecting your ability to perform daily tasks or maintain a regular routine?

Yeah… it is. I mean, I’m still getting some things done, but not in the normal way. I missed a design review at work, which was really embarrassing because that’s the kind of thing I’m usually on top of—or at least I try to look like I am.

And then at home it’s like… I’ll start doing one thing, notice something else, and somehow I’m standing in the hallway holding a mug and not remembering why I went there. Which sounds like a sitcom thing, except it’s not funny when it’s your actual day. And then because I feel so scattered, I avoid people. Friends, family… I keep putting off texts and calls because I don’t want them to hear how unreliable I’ve been lately. So yeah, my routine’s definitely been affected.
Have you noticed your mood swings affecting your work or school performance in any way?

Yeah, work has definitely taken a hit. I missed a design review, which… I keep replaying because that’s exactly the sort of thing I’m supposed to be reliable about. And then I start thinking about how everyone probably noticed, and then I’m not just worried about work, I’m avoiding messages from friends and family too because I feel embarrassed.

It’s like once I seem scattered in one place, I start assuming I seem that way everywhere. So yes—my work performance has been affected, mostly in that I’m not showing up the way I normally would, and I’ve felt really unreliable lately.
Do you find that your mood swings follow a consistent pattern or cycle throughout the day or week?

I don’t know if it’s like… a neat daily or weekly cycle, exactly. I’ve tried to figure that out, because I like patterns—my job is basically staring at patterns until they make sense—but this doesn’t feel that tidy.

What I can say is the whole intense up-and-down thing has really been going on since I moved into this apartment, so… about a month ago. Which makes me wonder if it’s the move, or the space, or just timing. I keep thinking maybe once I finish unpacking the last boxes it’ll settle down, but then I realize I’ve been saying that for weeks.
Do you think your mood swings might be related to your menstrual cycle?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really tracked it that way. I mean, I’ve had moments where I think, “Oh, maybe this is hormonal,” but then I also think that about stress, or the apartment, or not sleeping right, or—well, then I start making a whole spreadsheet in my head and never actually make the spreadsheet.

So… I don’t know. I haven’t noticed a clear connection to my cycle, but I also haven’t been paying close enough attention to say for sure.
Have you ever had a period where you felt so good or irritable that you didn't need to sleep for several days?

Yeah… there have been a few nights like that. Not like I stayed up for fun exactly—well, partly, because I’d start doing one thing and then suddenly it was 2 a.m., and then I’d think, “Okay, I can still get up early and answer emails,” or reorganize files, or whatever.

For several nights I think I only slept maybe three or four hours, and I’d wake up feeling like I was totally fine, like I should use the extra time to get ahead. Which is not really how I usually feel on that little sleep. Normally I’d be useless.
Have you found it difficult to carry out daily activities due to these mood swings?

Yeah… yes, I think so. I keep wanting to say “not really” because I’m still getting things done, sort of, but then I think about it and… I missed a design review, which is not like me. I had it on my calendar and everything, and somehow I just—my brain was everywhere.

And I’ve been kind of avoiding people, too. Friends, my family. Not because they did anything, just because I feel embarrassed. Like I’ve been so scattered and unreliable lately that I don’t want to have to explain myself, so I just don’t answer right away, and then it becomes this whole bigger thing.
Have you felt like your mood swings are affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah… I think it is, even if part of me wants to say I’m managing. Like, I still show up to work most of the time and I can make things look okay on the surface, but then something happens—like I missed that design review—and it’s like, okay, that actually affects my life.

And then socially, I’ve been sort of disappearing. I keep not answering friends or my family because I feel embarrassed, like they’re going to notice I’ve been scattered and kind of unreliable. Which is silly maybe, because then avoiding them makes me feel worse, but… yeah. I think it’s been affecting my quality of life.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or irritable and your thoughts were racing, and this lasted for at least a few days?

Yeah… earlier this month, I think. It’s hard to describe because part of it felt good, like I was almost electric, really upbeat, like everything was moving fast and I could handle it.

But then I’d switch really quickly. Like a contractor was late getting back to me about something small, and I snapped at him like he was deliberately trying to derail me. And I did the same with my sister over some tiny delay—honestly, I don’t even remember why it felt so urgent. It just felt, in the moment, like people were blocking me on purpose.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or irritable and your thoughts were racing for at least four consecutive days?

Yeah, earlier this month… I think it was at least a few days, yes. I felt almost electric, like really upbeat and fast, and then the smallest thing would flip me into being so irritated.

Like a contractor took too long to get back to me—honestly it was probably a normal delay, people have other jobs, emails pile up, I know that—but in the moment I snapped like he was personally blocking me. And I did something similar with my sister over some tiny delay too. It felt so urgent at the time, like everyone was getting in my way.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think it is, even if part of me wants to say I’m managing. Like, I still show up to work most of the time and I can make things look okay on the surface, but then something happens—like I missed that design review—and it’s like, okay, that actually affects my life.

And then socially, I’ve been sort of disappearing. I keep not answering friends or my family because I feel embarrassed, like they’re going to notice I’ve been scattered and kind of unreliable. Which is silly maybe, because then avoiding them makes me feel worse, but… yeah. I think it’s been affecting my quality of life.

doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or irritable and your thoughts were racing, and this lasted for at least a few days?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Earlier this month I felt almost electric and upbeat one minute, then snapped at a contractor or my sister over tiny delays like they were personally trying to block me.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about periods of extremely high or irritable mood lasting several days; this item directly covers elevated or irritable mood episodes.

patient.answer:
Yeah… earlier this month, I think. It’s hard to describe because part of it felt good, like I was almost electric, really upbeat, like everything was moving fast and I could handle it.

But then I’d switch really quickly. Like a contractor was late getting back to me about something small, and I snapped at him like he was deliberately trying to derail me. And I did the same with my sister over some tiny delay—honestly, I don’t even remember why it felt so urgent. It just felt, in the moment, like people were blocking me on purpose.
